prompt.adult: Paul asks what advantage his hardships would be if the dead do not rise. According to 15:32, what had he fought with at Ephesus?
prompt.child: Paul says he faced great danger at Ephesus. What does he say he fought with there?
prompt.teen: 1 Corinthians 15:32: “I have fought with” what “at Ephesus”?
prompt.older: According to 1 Corinthians 15:32, what did Paul fight with at Ephesus?

verses.text: If, in the manner of men, I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantage is it to me? If the dead do not rise, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”

explanation.child: Look near the start of verse 32.
explanation.teen: 15:32 says what he fought and where, then asks a question. Read the first part.
explanation.older: It follows “I have fought with” in 15:32.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:32 then quotes a saying: “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
teaching.takeaway: I have fought with beasts at Ephesus.

prompt.adult: Paul says he is not worthy to be called an apostle, because he persecuted the church of God. What does he call himself in 15:9?
prompt.child: Paul felt unworthy because he had once hurt the church. How does he describe himself among the apostles?
prompt.older: According to 1 Corinthians 15:9, how does Paul describe himself?

verses.text: For I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 9.
explanation.teen: 15:9 says what he is, then why he is not worthy. Read the first part.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:10 says, “But by the grace of God I am what I am.”
teaching.takeaway: I am the least of the apostles.

prompt.adult: After James and all the apostles, Christ was seen last of all by Paul. According to 15:8, as what?
prompt.child: Paul says the risen Christ appeared to him last of all. How does he describe himself?
prompt.teen: 1 Corinthians 15:8: “Then last of all He was seen by me also, as by” whom?
prompt.older: According to 1 Corinthians 15:8, how does Paul describe himself as a witness?

choices.text: one born out of due time
one sent from a far country

verses.text: After that He was seen by James, then by all the apostles.
Then last of all He was seen by me also, as by one born out of due time.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 8.
explanation.teen: 15:7 names earlier witnesses; 15:8 says who saw Him last, then how Paul describes himself. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:7 says He was seen by James, then by all the apostles.
teaching.takeaway: He was seen by me also, as by one born out of due time.

prompt.adult: Paul says that if Christ is not risen, faith is futile. According to 15:19, what are we, if in this life only we have hope in Christ?
prompt.child: Paul says hope in Christ is not only for this life. If it were, what would believers be?
prompt.teen: 1 Corinthians 15:19: “we are of all men” what?
prompt.older: According to 1 Corinthians 15:19, what would we be if our hope in Christ were for this life only?

verses.text: And if Christ is not risen, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins!
If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men the most pitiable.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 19.
explanation.teen: 15:17 gives one result; 15:19 gives a condition, then another result. Read the end of 15:19.
explanation.older: It follows “we are of all men” in 15:19.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:17 adds, “you are still in your sins!”
teaching.takeaway: We are of all men the most pitiable.

prompt.adult: Paul answers the question of how the dead are raised. According to 15:36, what you sow is not made alive unless what happens?
prompt.child: Paul uses grain that is planted to explain the resurrection. What must happen before it can be made alive?
prompt.teen: 1 Corinthians 15:36: “what you sow is not made alive” unless what?
prompt.older: According to 1 Corinthians 15:36, what must happen to what is sown before it is made alive?

verses.text: Foolish one, what you sow is not made alive unless it dies.
And what you sow, you do not sow that body that shall be, but mere grain—perhaps wheat or some other grain.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 36.
explanation.teen: 15:36 says what you sow is not made alive, then gives a condition. 15:37 speaks of mere grain. Read the condition.
explanation.older: It follows “is not made alive” in 15:36.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:37 says you do not sow the body that shall be, but mere grain, perhaps wheat.
teaching.takeaway: What you sow is not made alive unless it dies.

prompt.adult: In 15:14 Paul asks what follows if Christ is not risen. In 15:58, what does he say believers know about their labor in the Lord?
prompt.child: Paul tells believers to keep working for the Lord. What does he say their work is?
prompt.teen: 1 Corinthians 15:58: “knowing that your labor is” what “in the Lord”?
prompt.older: Linking 1 Corinthians 15:14 with 15:58, what does Paul say about labor in the Lord?

verses.text: And if Christ is not risen, then our preaching is empty and your faith is also empty.
Therefore, my beloved brethren, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 58.
explanation.teen: 15:14 is the setting; 15:58 gives commands, then what they know. Read what they know.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:58 calls them to be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.
teaching.takeaway: Your labor is not in vain in the Lord.

prompt.adult: In 15:22 Paul writes that as in Adam all die. In 15:45, what did the last Adam become?
prompt.child: Paul compares the first man with Christ, the last Adam. What did the last Adam become?
prompt.older: Alongside 15:22, what does 15:45 say the last Adam became?

verses.text: For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ all shall be made alive.
And so it is written, “The first man Adam became a living being.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.

explanation.child: Look at the end of verse 45.
explanation.teen: 15:22 is the setting; 15:45 quotes what is written about the first man, then speaks of the last. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “The last Adam became” in 15:45.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:22 says that in Christ all shall be made alive. 15:45 first quotes, “The first man Adam became a living being.”
teaching.takeaway: The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.

prompt.adult: In 15:12 Paul asks how some say there is no resurrection of the dead. In 15:52, how quickly does he say we shall be changed?
prompt.child: Paul says believers will be changed very quickly. In how long?
prompt.older: Alongside 15:12, how quickly does 15:52 say the change will come?

choices.text: the space of a single breath
a single beat of the heart
the blink of a lamp flame

verses.text: Now if Christ is preached that He has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 52.
explanation.teen: 15:12 is the question; 15:52 opens with two phrases about how quickly. Read the second.
explanation.older: It follows “in a moment, in” in 15:52.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:12 says Christ is preached as raised from the dead. 15:52 says the dead will be raised incorruptible.
teaching.takeaway: We shall be changed in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye.
